verdict.rationale: 2FAS advertises 'Freedom to self-host your data' and lets users store encrypted vault files via their own cloud, WebDAV, or external drive rather than mandatory 2FAS-hosted storage ([2fas-docs-14],[2fas-docs-5]), which gives IT admins some ability to keep secrets within their own infrastructure. However, there is no documented dedicated self-hostable 'sync server' application, deployment guide, or architecture reference — it's storage-location flexibility (WebDAV/cloud/file) rather than a full self-managed sync service, and a community reviewer questions how this differs from a true self-hosted server like Bitwarden ([2fas-comm-1]). Missing for 10: dedicated self-hosted sync-server software/binary, admin deployment/config docs, and independent verification that no external 2FAS infrastructure is involved in sync.
